LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 2.3.1 WORD CLASSES: NOUNS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.3: Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns, part of Strand 2 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why are some things impossible to count? 2. How can you group things that cannot be counted?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: Learners develop the skill of teamwork as they create posters and poems, and share them on the

classroom wall.

● Self-efficacy: Learners develop the skill of negotiation as they pick out count, non-count, singular, and plural nouns from newspapers

and magazine articles.

Values:
● Unity: is enhanced as learners work together to identify the different types of nouns in the classroom.

● Respect: is achieved as learners take turns to work in groups to create poems and posters.

Link to other Subjects

The learner relates the concept of count and non-count nouns to their learning of nouns in Kiswahili.
